heroSub: 10 hand-picked Nonthaburi hotels across every budget — from hotels next to IMPACT in Muang Thong Thani and stays on the Pink Line that walk into Central, to a Chao Phraya riverside resort and budget rooms on the Purple Line. Covering Muang Thong, Chaengwattana, Tiwanon, Tha Nam Non and Bang Yai. From roughly ฿600–2,300/night.
heroStats: 🏨 5 key areas (Muang Thong·Chaengwattana·Tiwanon·Tha Nam Non·Bang Yai)
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right area in Nonthaburi matter so much?
introHtml: Nonthaburi borders Bangkok, and most people stay here for a reason rather than for sightseeing — a fair or concert at IMPACT, business at the Chaengwattana government complex, or simply a cheaper metro-side base than the city centre. Stays fall into several areas with very different feels — Muang Thong Thani (Pak Kret) is the IMPACT events hub, best for fairs and concerts; Chaengwattana sits on the Pink Line metro and Central department store, handy for government-office errands; Tiwanon–Tha Nam Non runs along the Chao Phraya near the Purple Line, good if you want a river view; and Bang Yai is next to Central WestGate at the end of the Purple Line, best for tight budgets. Many people book without checking the area and end up stuck in Chaengwattana traffic or shuttling in and out all day. This guide rounds up 10 hand-picked Nonthaburi hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Nonthaburi borders Bangkok and has two metro lines running through it, so it's easy to pick an area by the line. The Purple Line (Tao Poon–Khlong Bang Phai) runs through Khae Rai, Tiwanon, Tha Nam Non and Bang Yai, connecting to the Blue Line at Tao Poon for Bangkok. The Pink Line (Khae Rai–Min Buri) runs through Chaengwattana and Pak Kret, with a station outside Central Chaengwattana and a branch into Muang Thong Thani–IMPACT. Pick by your plan: Muang Thong Thani — walk to the IMPACT halls and concert venues (Novotel, ibis); Chaengwattana — on the Pink Line and Central, near the government complex (Wanda Grand, Hop Inn); Tiwanon–Tha Nam Non — on the Chao Phraya near the Purple Line and the ferry pier (Riverine Place, Kalanan, Bed by Boat, Nonthaburi Palace, Humz); Bang Yai — the end of the Purple Line next to Central WestGate (The Grand Residence). Almost every hotel has parking, so they suit both drivers and metro riders.

entries.name: ibis Bangkok IMPACT
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Popular Rd · Muang Thong Thani · Pak Kret
entries.addr: Popular Rd, Muang Thong Thani, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi
entries.storyHtml: ibis Bangkok IMPACT is the stay that best balances the highest score with the most reviews in this guide — 9.3 from 1,684 reviews. It's a 3-star Accor hotel right next to the Novotel in Muang Thong Thani, with a skywalk straight into the IMPACT Exhibition Center so you never step into the sun. Guests consistently praise the clean rooms, soft beds and good service, at a price well below the 4-star next door. A strong fit if you're at a fair or concert at IMPACT and want to keep costs down.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rates spike on big IMPACT event dates — book early and lock the price in, which works out far cheaper than booking at the last minute.

Skywalk to IMPACT, no need to step outside
Clean rooms, soft beds, good service
Cheaper than the 4-star hotels in Muang Thong
cons: Plain, compact rooms in standard ibis style

entries.name: Best Western Plus Wanda Grand Hotel

entries.addr: Chaengwattana Rd, Khlong Kluea, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Best Western Plus Wanda Grand is the 4-star that fits best for anyone with business around Chaengwattana, scoring 9.0 from 959 reviews. Its edge is location — about 280 metres from the Pink Line's Chaengwattana–Pak Kret 28 station, with a covered walk into Central Chaengwattana. Rooms start at a roomy 30 sqm, there's a pool and gym, and the staff draw the most praise in reviews. A solid pick for meetings, conferences or government-office errands.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Take the Pink Line outside the hotel instead of driving — it beats the Chaengwattana traffic — and ask for a higher-floor city-view room, which is quieter.

entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Chaengwattana is the budget hotel that punches above its price — 9.2 from 177 reviews. It's a budget chain selling clean simplicity: bright rooms, soft beds and a quiet night from just ฿900. It sits in Chaengwattana near the Pink Line and the government complex, with easy onward travel to Muang Thong or IMPACT. A fit for anyone who just wants a clean, well-located room at a light price, with no pool or extras to pay for.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Hop Inn doesn't serve breakfast, but Chaengwattana is full of convenience stores and eateries nearby — easy to find food on foot.

entries.name: Novotel Bangkok IMPACT
entries.revCount: 1,629 reviews · scores 8.9 · next to IMPACT Arena
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Popular Rd · Muang Thong Thani · Pak Kret
entries.addr: Popular Rd, Ban Mai, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Novotel Bangkok IMPACT is the 380-room 4-star that's the first name for anyone with business at IMPACT, scoring 8.9 from 1,629 reviews. Its draw is walking to IMPACT Arena, Challenger and the event halls without a car, plus an indoor pool, spa, gym, The Square buffet and a kids' club all under one roof. A fit for fairs, concerts, conferences or families who want a 4-star room with full facilities. Rates climb hard on big event dates.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a lake-view room toward Muang Thong's lake when booking, and on big event days leave extra time to check in. Use a ride-hailing app rather than flagging a taxi out front.

entries.storyHtml: Humz Canal Stay is a wooden house on Khlong Om Non that sells a quiet canalside mood, with just 4 water-view rooms, scoring 9.0 from 48 reviews. Its standout is a stylish wooden design right on the canal, peaceful and cut off from the city — a fit for couples or anyone after a slow-living break without going far. With so few rooms it fills fast, and rates rise on holidays and in high season. Best for travellers after a riverside experience over big-hotel convenience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms are very limited and the score is high, so it books up fast on holidays — reserve ahead, and plan to come by car since it's down a canalside lane.

entries.storyHtml: Nonthaburi Palace Hotel is the best-value in-town option around Khae Rai–Tiwanon, scoring 8.7 from 149 reviews. It starts at just ฿800 in the heart of Mueang Nonthaburi, near the Purple Line and the provincial government office. There are 2024-refurbished rooms in noticeably better shape than the older ones, plus parking. A fit for anyone with errands in central Nonthaburi or after a light-priced base that connects to Bangkok by metro.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Go for a Deluxe from the 2024 refurbishment — it's only a few hundred baht more but clearly newer and better-kept than the older rooms.

It sits near Nonthaburi pier and the Purple Line, so you can take the Chao Phraya express boat or the metro into Bangkok. faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Nonthaburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: It depends on your errands and how you'll get around. Muang Thong Thani (Pak Kret) is best if you have business at IMPACT, with a walk to the event halls (ibis, Novotel). Chaengwattana is on the Pink Line and Central, near the government complex (Wanda Grand, Hop Inn). Tiwanon–Tha Nam Non runs along the Chao Phraya near the Purple Line and the ferry pier (Riverine Place, Bed by Boat, Nonthaburi Palace, Humz). Bang Yai is at the end of the Purple Line next to Central WestGate (The Grand Residence).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Nonthaburi hotels cost?
faq.a: There's a wide range: budget hotels and apartments start around ฿600–900 (The Grand Residence, Nonthaburi Palace, Bed by Boat, Hop Inn); midrange to 4-star hotels and resorts run about ฿1,200–2,300 (Riverine Place, Wanda Grand, Kalanan, ibis, Novotel); a design canal stay like Humz Canal Stay starts around ฿2,300. Prices around Muang Thong–Chaengwattana spike on big IMPACT event dates.

faq.q: ❓ I'm here for an IMPACT event in Muang Thong Thani — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you have a fair, concert or conference at IMPACT, stay in Muang Thong Thani so you can walk to the venue. ibis Bangkok IMPACT ฿1,200 is the most reviewed at 9.3, with a skywalk to IMPACT — best for tight budgets. Novotel Bangkok IMPACT ฿2,300 is a 4-star next to IMPACT Arena with an indoor pool, spa and buffet — best for families and travellers who want facilities. Both spike on big event dates, so book ahead.

faq.q: ❓ Which Nonthaburi hotels are on the metro?
faq.a: Nonthaburi has two metro lines. On the Pink Line (Chaengwattana–Pak Kret) are Best Western Plus Wanda Grand (about 280 m from the station) and Hop Inn Chaengwattana. Near the Purple Line (Khae Rai–Tiwanon–Tha Nam Non–Bang Yai) are Nonthaburi Palace, Riverine Place, Bed by Boat and The Grand Residence Bang Yai. Picking a stay on a metro line connects to Bangkok far more easily than driving.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay for a Chao Phraya river view in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: Nonthaburi has riverside stays across several tiers. Kalanan Riverside Resort ฿1,800 is a boutique riverside resort on the Pak Kret side with a pool and river-view rooms. Riverine Place ฿1,200 has big rooms with a kitchen, some with a river view, near Nonthaburi pier. Bed by Boat ฿800 is a budget option in Tha Nam Non near the Chao Phraya express-boat pier. And Humz Canal Stay ฿2,300 is a wooden house on Khlong Om Non for a quiet mood.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Nonthaburi hotel?
faq.a: On normal weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But during big IMPACT events in Muang Thong Thani — motor shows, book fairs or concerts — rooms around Muang Thong and Chaengwattana fill very fast and rates climb, so book a month or more ahead. Small-room stays like Humz Canal Stay also fill fast on holidays, so reserve early there too.
